title: Jogae Gui Grilled Clams
shortDescription: Live hard-shell clams are scrubbed, grilled covered until they open, and finished with garlic-scallion butter; every non-opening clam is discarded.
culturalContext: Jogae gui broadly means grilled shellfish and may include varied species, table-grill service, sauces, and coastal restaurant presentations. This draft narrows the method to sourced live hard-shell clams and requires species-specific review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.item: live hard-shell clams from an approved source
ingredients.preparation: shells intact and closed or closing when tapped

instructions.heading: Verify source and life
instructions.action: Check the harvest tag or source label; discard cracked clams and any open clam that does not close when tapped.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the source tag or label and buy only from an approved supplier.

instructions.heading: Scrub briefly
instructions.action: Scrub shells under cool running water and drain; do not soak in fresh water.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shell surfaces are free of grit.
instructions.safetyNote: Prevent shellfish liquid from contacting ready-to-eat food.

instructions.heading: Prepare finish
instructions.action: Mix butter, garlic, scallions, and optional gochugaru in a clean bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the clean finishing mixture away from raw shellfish and utensils.

instructions.heading: Preheat and arrange
instructions.action: Preheat grill to medium-high, place clams hinge-side down on a grill-safe tray, and close the lid.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Clams sit steadily in one layer.
instructions.safetyNote: Use heatproof gloves and keep the grill outdoors due to heat and smoke.

instructions.heading: Cook until open
instructions.action: Cook 6 to 10 minutes, removing each clam with clean tongs as it opens fully.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shells open and clam meat is opaque and firm.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard every clam that does not open during cooking; never pry it open to eat.

instructions.heading: Finish and serve
instructions.action: Add a small amount of clean garlic-scallion butter to opened clams, heat 1 minute, and serve immediately in a clean bowl.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Butter melts and clams remain steaming hot.
instructions.safetyNote: Shells and trapped liquid are extremely hot; warn diners and discard chipped shell pieces.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor covered grill at medium-high heat with clams in a stable grill-safe tray; segregate raw-shellfish tools from clean serving tools.
foodSafetyNotes: Retain the harvest tag or source label and use only live shellfish from an approved source.
Discard cracked clams and any clam that is open before cooking and does not close when tapped.
Cook until shells open; discard every non-opening clam.
Higher-risk people should avoid raw or undercooked shellfish; this draft serves clams fully cooked.
Prevent raw shellfish and liquid from contacting ready-to-eat food.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Do not substitute a different shellfish species without species-specific handling review.
Use a verified dairy-free finishing fat if needed.
ingredientSourcing: Buy live clams cold from an approved source with a harvest tag or source label.
Reject cracked shells, off odors, or clams that fail the tap test.
makeAhead: Mix the finish up to 1 day ahead; clean clams immediately before cooking.
storage: Store live clams at or below 40°F / 4°C in a breathable container; do not seal airtight or submerge in fresh water.
reheating: Reheating can toughen clams; if retained, reheat rapidly to 165°F / 74°C and discard any questionable shellfish.
leftovers: Remove cooked meat from shells, refrigerate within 2 hours in a shallow covered container, and use within 1 day.
servingSuggestions: Serve immediately with a bowl for empty shells.
Warn diners about hot shells and possible fragments.

faq.question: What if a clam stays closed?
faq.answer: Discard it. Do not pry open or eat a clam that failed to open during cooking.

faq.question: Should I soak clams in fresh water?
faq.answer: No. This draft uses a brief scrub under running water and no fresh-water soak.
